\section{Data}\label{app:data}
All numbers in this appendix were produced by the procedures of \cref{app:algorithms}; the certificates in \cref{app:data-cert} can be checked by hand or by a short independent program.
\subsection{Exact counts}\label{app:data-counts}
\Cref{tab:counts} lists $\Ham(n)$, the number of undirected Hamiltonian paths of $G(n)$, for
$15\le n\le75$. Values for $n\le56$ were first obtained with Graphillion; the dynamic program of
\cref{alg:frontier} extended the computation to $n=75$.
For $n\le14$, $\Ham(n)=0$ since $G(n)$ is disconnected.

\subsection{Glue arrangements}\label{app:data-glue}
Notation as in \cref{tab:glue}: a bracket $[x\ y]$ is a lifted segment traversed from $x$ to $y$, and
other entries are glue vertices. Every junction sum has been checked to be a square. The arrangement
of \cref{tab:glue} ($t=5$, $(u,w)=(1,3)$, $n$ odd) is the one used in \cref{thm:main}. The others
support \cref{prop:t3}.

\subsection{Numerical tables}\label{app:numerics}
\paragraph{The constant $C$ (\cref{alg:sinkhorn-cont}).}
\[\begin{array}{rcc}M & C & \text{max residual}\\400 & -0.6325467 & 2.2e-16\\1600 & -0.6325390 & 3.3e-16\\3200 & -0.6325383 & 2.2e-16\end{array}\]
Also $B=\frac{\sqrt2}2-\frac32\log(1+\sqrt2)=-0.6149536$ and $\log\iint\kappa=-0.5936915$.
\paragraph{Edge counts (\cref{alg:edges}).}
\[\begin{array}{rrcc}n & e(G(n)) & e/n^{3/2} & e(G(n)[4\mathbb{Z}])\big/\tfrac1{16}e(G(n))\\10^{4} & 276100 & 0.276100 & 1.9990\\10^{6} & 276141896 & 0.276142 & 2.0000\\10^{8} & 276142369768 & 0.276142 & 2.0000\end{array}\]with $\frac23(\sqrt2-1)=0.276142$.
\paragraph{The finite Bregman bound (\cref{alg:bregman}).} Normalised value $\bigl(\log\mathrm{UB}(n)-\log n!+\frac n2\log n\bigr)/n$, which tends to $B$ slowly:
\[\begin{array}{rrr}n & \log\mathrm{UB}(n) & \text{normalised}\\25 & 19.20 & +0.0572\\50 & 47.50 & -0.0635\\75 & 80.59 & -0.1252\\100 & 116.77 & -0.1671\\1000 & 2032.21 & -0.4260\\10000 & 30632.62 & -0.5425\end{array}\]
\paragraph{Bethe lower bound for cycle covers (\cref{alg:bethe}).}
\[\begin{array}{rc}n & (F(S)-\frac n2\log n)/n\\1000 & -1.60375\\4000 & -1.61752\\16000 & -1.62498\\64000 & -1.62871\\\infty & C-1=-1.63254\end{array}\]
\paragraph{Residuals (\cref{alg:predictor}).}
$r_C(n)=\log\Ham(n)-[\log(n!/2)-\frac{n-1}2\log n+Cn]$ (the constant-$C$ formula of \cref{tab:resid})
and $r_S(n)=\log\Ham(n)-\log\widehat\Ham(n)$ (the scaling predictor of \cref{subsec:barvinok}). For
$n\le30$, $r_S$ is undefined, because the Sinkhorn scaling does not exist.
